Brijesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Prin. Secy. ... on 23
March, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 687 of 2023
Applicant :- Brijesh Kumar

Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
Heard Shri Amit Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Brijesh Kumar in Case Crime/F.I.R. No. 002 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Musafirkhana, District Amethi, with the prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the applicant while pressing the anticipatory bail application submits that it is a case of false implication and the applicant has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

It is further submitted that the allegations levelled against the applicant are to the tune that he has misappropriated certain amount which was paid by the State Government to the victim of sexual assault by opening bank account of the victim by providing his mobile phone number and by using his mobile phone and mobile number amount was transferred by him to his bank account as well as in the bank account of one Ram Dhani.

Highlighting the above facts, it is vehemently submitted that the victim of sexual assault is illiterate and it was she, who had provided the mobile number of the applicant in the bank along with the Brijesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Prin. Secy. ... on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185096150/
1 bank account opening form and the applicant has not provided his mobile number to the bank.
It is also submitted that the amount has been withdrawn by the victim of sexual assault/informant herself and it was she, who has used the mobile phone of the applicant in transferring the amount.
It is next submitted that criminal history of three cases has been adequately explained in the affidavit enclosed with the anticipatory bail application and the alleged offences against the applicant are triable by Magistrate and applicant is ready to co-operate in the investigation.

sentences.text:
Thus,
protection from arrest be granted to the instant applicant.

Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that applicant is having criminal history of five cases,
moreover, the investigating officer during the course of investigation has recorded the statement of the Branch Manager of Bank of Baroda, Branch Musafirkhana, District Amethi, namely, Shri Arvind Kumar Mehta, who has elaborately stated about the money which has been transferred by the instant applicant in his bank account as well as in the bank account of one Ram Dhani on various occasions and having regard to the fact that the Mobile No. 7752883837 is admitted to the applicant, as his mobile number, he is not entitled for any protection.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it would be evident that allegations of misappropriating the compensation money given to the victim of sexual assault has been levelled against the applicant by opening her bank account by providing his (accused applicant) phone number and thereafter by creating a U.P.I. or Bank App transferring of money on different occasions to his bank account and to the bank account of Ram Dhani.

Perusal of the statement of the Manager of the Bank of Baroda, Branch Musafirkhana, District Amethi recorded by the investigating officer, would reveal that the applicant had transferred Rs.
50,000/- from the account of the victim of sexual assault/informant to his account on 02.04.2021 and on the same day Rs. 40,000/- were transferred by him to his own account through I.M.P.S. and thereafter Rs. 10,000/- were transferred to the bank account of one Ram Dhani and on 06.04.2021 Rs. 50,000/- were transferred by him to the bank account of Ram Dhani and Rs. 49,500/- to his own account on 07.07.2021, apart from withdrawing Rs. 100/- on 08.04.2021.

It is also stated by the Bank Manager that the informant/victim of sexual assault has also withdrawn cash to the tune of Rs.5000/- on 09.04.2021, Rs. 10,000/- on 09.04.2021, Rs. 10,000/- on 12.04.2021, Rs. 10,000/- on 12.04.2021, Rs. 5000/- on 13.04.2021 and on 15.04.2021 she had recharged D.T.H. Device and on 16.04.2021 she has transferred Rs. 10,000/- and Rs. 5000/- to the bank account of the instant applicant and again on 19.04.2021 she has withdrawn cash of Rs.
10,000/-.

It is also stated by the Bank Manager that on 27.04.2021 the applicant has transferred Rs.
15,000/- to the bank account of Mahesh Kumar Maurya and after withdrawing Rs. 200/- by the applicant only Rs. 5/- had remained in the bank account of the victim/informant.

The statement of the Bank Manager would not leave any doubt that the compensation amount given by the State to the victim of sexual assault/informant has been misappropriated, by hatching a conspiracy by the instant applicant in connivance with other persons in whose bank account the money has been transferred by him, including one Ram Dhani, who at that point of time is stated to be posted as Sub Brijesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. sentences.text:
However, in the case diary which has been placed for the perusal of this Court,
there is no whisper as to how the amount of Rs. 50,000/- was transferred by the instant applicant- Brijesh Kumar in the bank account of a government servant/Sub Inspector of Police, namely, Ram Dhani, who at that point of time was posted at Police Station Musafirkhana, District Amethi, as the same should have been investigated by the investigating officer with the same vigour with which the allegations against the applicant are being investigated.

Thus, primafacie it appears to be a case where a big chunk of the compensation given by the State Government to the victim of sexual assault has been misappropriated by the instant applicant in connivance with a Sub Inspector of Police, namely, Ram Dhani, who at that point of time was posted at Police Station Musafirkhana, District Amethi.
Having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case placed herein-before, no case for exercising discretion in favour of the applicant is emerging.
Thus, the anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of the applicant- Brijesh Kumar is, hereby, rejected.

However, this Court could not turn in nelson's eye towards the involvement of the Sub Inspector Ram Dhani in the alleged crime, as Rs. 50,000/- are stated to have been transferred by the instant applicant-accused Brijesh Kumar in the bank account of Ram Dhani, who at that point of time was posted as Sub Inspector of Police and the same must be the subject matter of investigation.
Thus, a copy of this order be placed before the Superintendent of Police, Amethi with the direction that either he or an officer of the rank of Additional S.P. or Deputy S.P. shall supervise the investigation being conducted in this case in order to ensure a fair investigation.
The Senior Registrar of this Bench shall forthwith transmit a copy of this order to the Superintendent of Police, Amethi for compliance.
Order Date :- 23.3.2023/
Praveen
